haiku-low.q1: Up to 10,000 rows, the API returns the CSV directly and stores nothing. Above that, a background job builds it and emails a link.
haiku-low.q2: It returns the existing active export with 202 and starts nothing new. If its filters differ, the page shows a mismatch panel with Cancel.
haiku-low.q3: The emailed link lasts 24 hours from creation, capped by file expiry. The bucket's 7-day lifecycle rule deletes files; no cleanup job exists.
haiku-low.q4: Three attempts with 60s and 300s waits. After the last fails, the export is marked failed, the user is emailed, and the page shows failure.
haiku-low.q5: Report rows are read only from the read replica. Job state is written to the primary database.
haiku-low.q6: Stored in the report_exports table in the primary database. The page polls every 5 seconds while active, and reopening it fetches the latest export.
haiku-low.q7: It reads 1,000-row keyset pages from the replica, buffers 16 MB, and uploads multipart parts, never holding the whole report or using local disk.
haiku-low.q8: Nothing is visible until completion. The next attempt aborts the old upload and starts over under a new run token. Nothing resumes from saved progress.
haiku-low.q9: Filters and columns are stored on the report_exports row when created. The job receives only export_id and reads everything else from that row.
haiku-low.q10: A partial unique index on (user_id, report_id) where status is queued or running. The losing insert reads the winning row and returns it.
haiku-low.q11: Upload completed and row marked done first. Rerun with a finished file skips the build and sends the email only if unsent.
haiku-low.q12: Nothing is stored. The response is an error, such as a replica error or 60-second timeout; the user sees a message and clicks again.

sonnet.q1: Chosen by reports.row_count (unfiltered, read from replica): 10,000 or fewer = small path, the API builds the CSV and returns it in the same response (200 text/csv attachment), nothing stored. Over 10,000 up to 2,000,000 = large path: a report_exports row is created, a background job queued, 202 returned at once; the job writes the file to the exports bucket and emails a download link (valid 24h). Above 2,000,000 returns 413.
sonnet.q2: The click returns the existing active export (202) instead of starting a new one (after running reconcile/H3 on it; if H3 fails it as stale, a new export is created). The page compares the export's filters with the current URL; if different it shows 'An export with different filters is running' with a Cancel button. It is not rejected with 409 and nothing starts automatically.
sonnet.q3: The emailed link lasts 24 hours from creation: TTL = min(24h, file_expires_at - now). The page's Download button works for 24h from completed_at, then 410. The stored file is removed by the bucket's lifecycle rule 7 days after creation; no cleanup job is built and the sweep deletes no files.
sonnet.q4: Up to 3 attempts (waits 60 s before attempt 2, 300 s before attempt 3; each attempt limited to 30 min). After attempt 3 fails, the final-failure hook (unless the object already exists, then it marks done) marks the export failed with 'The export could not be built after 3 attempts.', sends the user one csv_export_failed email (report_id, export_id, error_summary), and the page shows 'The export failed.' with a button to start a new export. Raw error goes to logs only.
sonnet.q5: The read replica only (page reads, row_count, rebuilt_at). Job state (report_exports) is written only to the primary.
sonnet.q6: Status is stored in the report_exports table on the primary database (status queued/running/done/failed, attempt, etc.). The page polls GET /api/reports/{report_id}/exports/latest every 5 seconds while the latest export is active, stopping at done, failed or none. On page load it fetches the latest export, so a returning user sees the state (done/expired/failed). The poll also runs reconcile (H3).
sonnet.q7: It streams: reads keyset pages of 1,000 rows from the replica, formats them into a 16 MB in-memory buffer, uploads each full buffer as a multipart part, clears it, and uploads the remainder as the final part. No whole report in memory, no local disk. Estimated memory about 60 MB average (about 100 MB worst case) versus a design target under 200 MB of the 512 MB; roughly 60 parts at average row size. Benchmark gate requires under 15 min and under 200 MB.
sonnet.q8: Nothing is visible at the final key until complete_multipart succeeds, so a half-written file is never downloadable. On an exception the attempt makes a best-effort abort_multipart then raises; if killed or the worker dies, the next attempt aborts the old upload (step 7.1) or the bucket's 24-hour rule discards unfinished uploads. There is no resume: the next attempt starts over from the beginning (new claim, new run token, new data_version, new key containing the run token, new multipart upload). Exception: if the earlier attempt already completed the visible object, the retry just marks the row done (H1) without rebuilding.
sonnet.q9: They are stored on the report_exports row (filters as a normalised query string, and cols) when it is inserted at the click. The queued job payload contains only {export_id}; the job loads the row and reads filters and cols from it (re-parsing them against the report's current columns). The export keeps those values even if the URL changes later.
sonnet.q10: A partial unique index on report_exports (user_id, report_id) WHERE status IN (queued, running), on the primary. The insert of the second request hits the index; it then reads the winning row and returns it with 202, so only one row is created.
sonnet.q11: Before the email: the multipart upload must be completed (object visible at file_key, verified via object_exists in H1) and the row conditionally updated to done (completed_at set); then H2 sends it, only if email_sent_at is null, and then sets email_sent_at. If the queue runs the job again: if status is done, it just calls H2 (sends the email only if not already sent, so no second email in normal cases) and returns; if the object exists but the row is not done, it calls H1 to mark done (without rebuilding or re-claiming) then emails once; if failed (cancelled/stale/duplicate) it returns without doing anything. A send that succeeds but whose email_sent_at write fails could cause a duplicate email (accepted).
sonnet.q12: Nothing is stored and nothing needs cleanup: the CSV is built fully in memory before the response starts, so no partial file can be delivered. The user gets an error (e.g. 503 too many builds, 413 too large, 409 report changed, replica error, or the 60-second API limit kill) and clicks again.
